title: The first balloon riders were a sheep, a duck and a rooster!
question: Did you know the first passengers in a hot-air balloon were a sheep, a duck and a rooster?
answer: On 19 September 1783, the first passengers in a hot-air balloon were a sheep, a duck and a rooster.

visual.what: A big colourful hot-air balloon floats in a blue sky. Below it a basket holds a fluffy sheep, a white duck and a red rooster, all peeking over the edge.

parts.text: Did you know the very first passengers in a hot-air balloon were a sheep, a duck and a rooster?

visual.what: France in 1783. Two men in old-fashioned clothes, the Montgolfier brothers, stand proudly next to a huge blue and gold balloon. A small calendar page reads 1783.

parts.text: It happened in France, in 1783. Two brothers, the Montgolfiers, built a huge balloon.

visual.what: Cutaway of a balloon. Small orange flames under the opening warm the air inside. Red dots inside the balloon are spread far apart, blue dots outside are close together. Arrows point up.

parts.text: Warm air inside lifted it. Hot air is lighter than cold air, so it rises.
Like a bubble going up in a pot of water!

visual.what: A wicker basket on the grass. Hùng carries the sheep, the duck on his head and the rooster under his arm, looking a bit flustered, with feathers flying.

parts.text: Nobody had flown in a balloon before. People were not sure what flying high would do to a living thing. So the animals went first to find out.
Oops! The duck is sitting on my head!

visual.what: The balloon rises over a crowd. A king and queen in fancy clothes wave from the ground. A ruler-style line shows about 480 metres of flight.

parts.text: On 19 September 1783, the balloon rose for the king and queen. It flew about 480 metres.

visual.what: A calendar flipping from September to November. A second balloon floats freely with two men waving from the basket.

parts.text: Soon after, people flew too. On 21 November 1783, two men took the first free flight.

visual.what: All four friends, Huy, Hùng, Bối and Beo, wave beside the balloon basket with the sheep, duck and rooster. A big Subscribe button with the words Ask Huy glows above them.

parts.text: So a sheep, a duck and a rooster were the first balloon riders! Follow Ask Huy for more wow facts!

facts.claim: The first passenger flight in a hot-air balloon was on 19 September 1783 and carried a sheep, a duck and a rooster.
The balloon was made by the Montgolfier brothers, and the animals flew for about 480 metres in front of the French king and queen.
Hot air is lighter (less dense) than cold air, so it rises, like a bubble of air in a pot of water.
The first flight carrying a person was on 15 October 1783 on a rope, and the first free flight was on 21 November 1783 with two men.
Many people think the animals were sent first as a safe test before people (a common historical explanation, not stated in the sources).

description: In 1783, before any person rode in a free balloon, a sheep, a duck and a rooster went up first. Learn why hot air rises and how the first flight went.
